note: 始まる is intransitive; 始める better matches starting or initiating something (ent_seq:1307550).
座る is the ordinary verb for sitting upright with the body supported by the buttocks; kneeling is a separate use.
少し commonly means a little; 少ない is the countable determiner/adjective sense few (ent_seq:1348910).
熱い is the standard adjective for an object having or giving off high temperature; 暑い is for weather or ambient heat.
気にかける directly expresses being concerned about or worrying about something (ent_seq:1221700).
なぜなら is a standard conjunction meaning because in an explanatory statement; its following reason clause is natural usage.
客 has a direct customer sense and is a natural everyday equivalent here; khách hàng is the standard Vietnamese business term.
hoạt động alone means activity or operation broadly; cách hoạt động expresses the method by which the device works.
客 and khách are standard equivalents for a guest; the hospitality and invitation context selects that shared sense.
塗る has a direct paint sense and sơn is the ordinary Vietnamese verb for applying paint.
調べる has a direct investigate sense and điều tra is a natural Vietnamese equivalent for ascertaining facts.
要求 leans toward a demand or request; 要件 directly means a requirement, requisite, or necessary condition (ent_seq:1546730).
指輪 and nhẫn specifically denote finger rings, while the stated sense also includes ear and nose jewelry; no single natural pair covers all three.
導く also covers abstract guidance; 手を引く has the specific sense lead by the hand (ent_seq:1896080).
文字 has a direct alphabet-letter sense in JMdict, and chữ cái is the standard Vietnamese term for a letter.
金融 emphasizes finance or credit activity; 財務 (ent_seq:1297000) better matches managing money and assets as financial affairs.
lạ can mean merely unfamiliar; kỳ quặc better expresses deviation from the normal and is attested as an adjective (vn_freq rank 6114).
欠陥 and lỗi both express a fault or malfunction in this stated sense; lỗi is the normal Vietnamese word for a fault.
部分 is a part or section; 取り分 directly denotes one's allocated share or portion (ent_seq:1654730).
井戸 and giếng denote water wells; 坑井 is limited to oil or gas wells, so no verified single equivalent covers the stated range.
農家 is a standard Japanese word glossed farmer, and nông dân is the ordinary Vietnamese term for a person engaged in farming.
そちら is polite and oriented toward the listener; そこ is the neutral general pronoun there (ent_seq:1006670).
どなた is polite; 誰 is the neutral everyday pronoun who (ent_seq:1416830).
The current adjective POS is incorrect for a lot as a quantity expression; determiner matches the listed quantifier use.
背中 is the common neutral word for the anatomical back (ent_seq:1472800); it is more natural here than the short form 背.
いかが is polite or formal; どう is the neutral general equivalent for how (ent_seq:1008910).
箱 means a box generally; ケース has a direct container sense and is used for commercial cases (ent_seq:1047880).
近く has the spatial sense near or close and works naturally as an adverb for leaving little distance.
傷 has a direct wound or injury sense, including cuts and tears; vết thương is the standard Vietnamese equivalent.
休み and the misspelled sự nghĩ ngơi mean rest generally; 睡眠 means sleep (ent_seq:1372370), and giấc ngủ is the natural Vietnamese noun.
あなた自身 makes the singular second-person emphasis explicit; 自身 is directly glossed yourself (ent_seq:1318000).
The うち sense centers on one's home or household; 家 read いえ is the neutral physical house or dwelling (ent_seq:1191730).
そろそろ often means it is about time; もうすぐ is the general soon or before-long adverb (ent_seq:2015610).
申す is humble speech; 言う is the neutral verb to say (ent_seq:1587040).
la hét can imply screaming; la is a common verb for shouting and is attested in the Vietnamese frequency list.
振る has a direct shake sense and lắc is the ordinary Vietnamese verb for moving something back and forth.
khuyến cáo is formal and often cautionary; khuyên is the general everyday verb to advise or counsel.
急ぐ and vội are natural equivalents for doing things quickly or being in a hurry.
振る also means shake or swing; 手を振る specifically means wave one's hand (ent_seq:1896090).
に対して directly expresses toward or in relation to someone or something (ent_seq:1009800), unlike the broad particle に.
